# deps/nonexistent-package

New dependency that does not exist on the registry.

A package added to package.json that does not exist on the registry it resolves to, looked up with --online, packages.online, or `ubon vet`, or whose name is not a valid npm package name (checked offline); also an unscoped name that exists on a private registry but not on npm.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: warn for an unscoped package that exists on the private registry in .npmrc but not on registry.npmjs.org (dependency confusion). Runs only when lookups are allowed; scoped packages that .npmrc maps to another registry are looked up there or skipped, never sent to the public registry.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Models invent plausible package names, and attackers register the names they invent (slopsquatting). A name nobody owns yet can be published by anyone before the next install.

## Flagged

`package.json` (block):

```json
"Bad Name": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"react-dom ": "^19.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"lodash/fp": "^4.17.21",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"@acme/": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
".hidden-utils": "^1.0.0",
```

## Not flagged

- Old Name: already at the base, not added in this change
- JSONStream: uppercase letters are valid in names published before npm required lowercase
- lodash.merge and @types/node: valid names
- my-dom: an npm alias whose target, react-dom, is a valid name
- notes-ui: a workspace package, not looked up on a registry
- Git Helper: a git dependency, not installed from a registry by that name
- react-markdown-pro-renderer and @vercel/ai-sdk-helpers: new names that may not exist, but lookups are off in this run, so the rule reports them under not checked instead of guessing
- zod: a valid new name; existence needs a registry lookup
- next: a version change, not a new package

## How to fix

Remove the dependency or correct its name, and check the package with `ubon vet <name>` before adding it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/nonexistent-package: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/nonexistent-package": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
